correctness.rationale: For four rank-three normals, a unique nonvanishing linear relation becomes positive after sign flips; a tetrahedron containing the origin gives four spherical face areas totaling 4π. Their polar triangle cells have areas 2π minus each face perimeter. L’Huilier and an explicit strict pair-averaging identity prove that every spherical triangle of area ≥π has perimeter ≥3acos(-1/3), equality only equilateral. Thus universal bound and rigidity; regular tetra yields exactly eight triangle cells and six larger quadrilateral cells. Source code reproduced 541 arrangements and 3000 smoothing comparisons, corroborative only.
